description: From writing the code and researching NASA data to designing the survival gameplay, the focus of my team is entirely on creating a fun experience for young players. The goal is to turn real space constraints into an exciting game where players hunt for parts while learning how to stay alive. Taking this on solo is a challenge, but it is awesome to build every piece of the mission from the ground up.
summary: Project Red Dawn: Train to Survive Mars is an interactive space-survival training simulation game built in Scratch. My project addresses the challenge "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" by making complex science and space concepts easy for young learners to understand. Instead of making them memorize chunks of facts, it provides a meaningful, hands-on experience of surviving on Mars through problem solving, decision making and gameplay. . Players cannot just rush blindly toward the goal, they must plan ahead and balance risk versus reward. Every game mechanic comes from real NASA research, from ECLSS life-support systems to hydrogen shielding and lava tunnel habitats. Overall, this inculcates strategic thinking skills and highlights the importance of careful planning. As humanity makes advancements in space exploration, this game fosters an early interest in aerospace engineering by making tough challenges feel achievable and fun.
details:
Project Red Dawn : Train to Survive Mars - Introduction

Learning about how astronauts survive on Mars often feels abstract when students only read about space hazards in textbooks.

This is an interactive Scratch survival game built for the Junior Astronaut Trainer challenge. Stranded on Mars after a meteor strike knocks their ship off course from Jupiter, players must search forward along the debris trail to recover three missing rocket parts as an Earth rescue window can only open every 26 months because that is how long it takes for Earth and Mars to align properly in their orbits leaving the astronaut helpless throughout that window.

Key survival mechanic include :

  • 5 Live Vitals: Oxygen, Suit Power, Radiation, Toxic Dust, and Bone Health.
  • Power & Suit Care: Generate power through solar energy, avoid over-sprinting so dust doesn't scratch suit seals, and keep base power running.
  • NASA Countermeasures: Shelter in Martian lava tubes, equip hydrogen shielding during solar flares, clean toxic dust on suit, and use the gym treadmill and weights to prevent low-gravity bone loss.

Working of Project

1. The spaceship loses power after crashing, so the astronaut uses solar energy to reboot communications and contact Earth for help though it drains a lot of power from a fragile system. Solar arrays are a primary power source for Mars surface missions (like NASA's InSight lander ). Once powered, astronauts use high-gain antennas to connect with orbiters that bounce signals back to Earth. Because Mars is so far away, radio signals take 3 to 22 minutes each way.

2. Next the player has to manage his vitals. Because Mars's atmosphere is 95% carbon dioxide, the astronaut relies on in-situ CO2 breakdown technology (like NASA's MOXIE system) to generate breathable oxygen, which drains rapidly if the player sprints continuously. At the same time, Martian dust accumulates and threatens equipment, while Mars's low gravity (only 38% of Earth's) causes rapid bone density loss that players must counter through regular exercise of treadmill running and weightlifting, just like real NASA astronauts.

3. The player is continuously at risk of radiation from solar events. Unlike Earth, Mars has no global magnetic field and a very thin atmosphere, leaving astronauts exposed. NASA research shows that underground volcanic caves (lava tunnels) act as natural radiation shelters, or use of hydrogen-rich materials (like water walls or polyethylene plastics) helps in absorbing space radiation and protection. Here the player can either stay unprotected in base, hide in lava tunnels or face high radiation if stayed out.

4. Players are penalized if they forget to turn power off before a solar flare and back on afterward or sprint carelessly causing wear and tear. If solar-powered space station closes power and forget to turn it on, oxygen production from carbon dioxide stops completely. This causes suffocation to them. Turning off the power station also closes the power supply to suit battery.

Benefits of Project

This project

  • Teaches complex space science through interactive gameplay rather than passive memorization.
  • Rewards attention to detail like such as powering down systems before solar storms, shows the real consequences of forgetfulness.
  • Makes tough engineering concepts feel fun and achievable, sparking early interest in STEM and space exploration.
  • Is built in Scratch, allowing anyone with a web browser to play, learn, and remix the code easily approachable to any user.

Impact of Project

Project Red Dawn: Train to Survive Mars provides experiential STEM learning that bridges the gap between textbook theory and real-world spaceflight. This helps build a generation of curious thinkers who feel ready to explore space and solve real-world challenges. Beyond aerospace facts, players walk away with practical habits like patience, careful planning, and calm problem-solving that help them succeed in school and everyday life. As humanity prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, this simulation empowers kids to see themselves not just as players, but as the future engineers and astronauts who will solve tomorrow's space challenges.

Tools and Technologies

  • SOFTWARE
  1. Scratch 3.0 (Block-Based Programming) and its sound library - Used as the core game engine to code all interactive mechanics
  2. Powerpoint shapes - Used to design custom UI elements, clean geometric buttons, gauges, and custom game graphics before exporting them as transparent sprites for Scratch.
  3. Canva editor - To design the final presentation slide deck
  4. NASA Open Science & Mission Resources - Provided authentic real-world Mars data (such as MOXIE oxygen generation, 38% gravity bone loss, and solar flare hazards) as well as public-domain spacecraft and habitat imagery.
  • HARDWARE
  1. Laptop - Served as the primary workstation to build the Scratch code, edit graphics, test game mechanics, and compile the presentation.
  2. Screen & Speakers - Used to inspect visual alignment, ensure UI readability for young learners, and test audio levels so emergency sound alerts create a clear sense of urgency.

Creativity of Project

My project is creative because it turns real NASA science into active survival rules instead of relying on plain text or quizzes. By combining forward exploration, multi-room transitions, and urgent sound effects, the game transforms a simple Scratch platform into a tense, realistic Mars simulation where players learn carefulness through real consequences. Instead of relying on a single linear path, the game gives players creative freedom to solve emergencies in multiple ways, such as sheltering inside volcanic lava tubes or managing solar power switches during incoming radiation storms. Even everyday habits like regular exercise and careful pacing are transformed into high-stakes survival mechanics that keep young learners engaged from start to finish.

Factors of Project

When designing the game, these key factors were checked:

  1. Scientific accuracy - Grounded every game mechanic in real NASA Mars research, scaling down real timelines for fun, fast and accurate gameplay.
  2. Game balance and fairness - Provided multiple survival choices like lava tunnels and base shielding, so emergencies feel challenging yet fair.
  3. Educational value over memorization - Designed active survival rules so players learn space science through real consequences instead of plain text.
  4. Accessibility and smooth performance - Designed active survival rules so players learn space science through real consequences instead of plain text.
  5. Immersive sensory feedback - Added urgent alert sounds and visual warnings to help players react quickly during solar flare emergencies.
  6. User Friendly: Designed intuitive on-screen buttons and clear vital bars so young learners can play without prior space knowledge.
